question: Do exact live-source index observations with EMA and pressure confirmation but no price breakout show enough subsequent movement to justify relaxing the v51 price-breakout requirement?

method.signal_source: frozen prospective v51 live-v3 observer decisions
method.candidate_definition: EMA alignment true, pressure confirmation true, price breakout false
method.overlap_control: all paths plus greedy non-overlapping path summary
method.friction_policy: twice the source-bound modeled taker entry fee plus entry slippage; descriptive symmetric round-trip sensitivity

decision.reason: Every horizon had negative mean after modeled friction for both measured source-native sides. SP500 had zero cost-clearing paths; SPCX was mixed and remained negative under all-path, independent-path, and largest-observation sensitivity.
decision.live_action: keep the exact v51 price-breakout requirement unchanged

confidence.basis: exact source-native prospective decisions and causal completed market paths, but only four SP500 and seven SPCX candidate observations
confidence.economic_edge_confidence: low because no executable entry quotes or completed v51 index lifecycles exist

reopen_condition: A predeclared later live-source window must materially expand independent price-only blocker observations and remain positive after source-bound costs, largest-winner removal, and side-specific analysis without weakening data or freshness contracts.
limitations: Decision close is not an executable entry quote.
Exit costs are a symmetric sensitivity derived from modeled entry costs because v51 has no index fills yet.
The study does not reproduce the active profit-lock or a complete lifecycle.
Small samples can miss a regime-specific effect.
No strategy, route, parameter, leverage, sizing, exit, or deployment behavior changed.

superseded_evidence.reason: The v1 generator did not exclude a terminal forming candle. The v2 generator is TDD-protected and includes only bars whose close time is at or before observed_at.
